questions.q: How does CloudWatch Logs organize log data?
options: Into log groups (per application/service), each containing log streams (per source instance or task)
Into a single flat list of all log lines across every AWS account
Into namespaces, the same structure CloudWatch Metrics uses
Into S3 buckets only, with no intermediate structure
questions.explain: A log group is typically one per application or service; within it, log streams separate log events by source instance, task, or container.

questions.q: For a containerized service on ECS, how do logs typically get into CloudWatch without extra application code?
options: Someone manually copies log files to S3 every hour
The awslogs driver ships container stdout/stderr directly into a log group
CloudWatch scrapes the container's filesystem nightly
Logs cannot be collected from containers
questions.explain: ECS's built-in awslogs log driver (and Container Insights for EKS) routes container stdout/stderr into CloudWatch Logs automatically.

questions.q: In a CloudWatch Logs Insights query, what does the `filter` command do?
options: Deletes matching log entries permanently
Narrows the result set to rows matching a condition, the same role as SQL's or KQL's WHERE
Changes the log group's retention period
Creates a new CloudWatch alarm
questions.explain: filter narrows rows based on a condition — functionally equivalent to KQL's where or SQL's WHERE clause.

questions.q: What does `stats avg(durationMs) as avgDuration by bin(5m)` compute?
options: The single average duration across all time, with no grouping
The average duration, grouped into 5-minute time buckets
The maximum duration recorded in the last 5 minutes only
A count of all log groups
questions.explain: bin(5m) groups rows into 5-minute buckets, and stats computes the average duration per bucket — the same aggregation pattern as KQL's summarize ... by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m).

questions.q: In the incident workflow this lesson describes, what role does Logs Insights play after a CloudWatch alarm fires?
options: It silences the alarm automatically
It lets you query the specific requests and messages behind the alarm's time window to find which requests failed and why
It replaces the need for alarms going forward
It only works for billing-related investigations
questions.explain: The alarm tells you a metric crossed a threshold (when). A Logs Insights query scoped to that window tells you which specific requests were involved and, via @message, why.
